issues.body: `collect_logical` emits every atomic leaf into one flat `Vec<DischargeObligation>` while discarding each `LogicalOperator`. For an `Or(A, B)` policy, a presentation need establish A or B, not both; for `Xone`, exactly-one semantics matters. Yet the API and docs describe the list as what a presentation "would have to establish", and the host has no rule/combinator structure from which to reconstruct the real requirement. The test `collects_obligations_nested_in_logical_constraints` uses an outer `Or` but expects both dimensions, making it vacuous with respect to the load-bearing decision semantics. Similar ambiguity exists for prohibitions: one emitted leaf alone does not make a multi-constraint prohibition fire.
issues.fix_hint: Return a structured discharge expression that preserves Atomic/And/Or/Xone nesting (and the distinction between top-level rule constraints and logical groups), or explicitly rename and document this API as a non-decisional inventory that must never be interpreted as required evidence. Add tests where AND, OR, and XONE produce distinguishable structures and show that a host can determine the valid evidence alternatives without consulting the original Policy.
issues.title: Flattening logical constraints destroys discharge semantics

verdict.summary: The extraction is not sound as the advertised decision interface because it flattens logical constraints and loses the AND/OR/XONE structure that determines which evidence is actually required. The added nested-OR test only checks that both leaves are emitted, so it confirms the information loss instead of validating a usable discharge requirement. A host consuming the returned flat list cannot distinguish alternatives from jointly required properties and can therefore over-require evidence or combine leaves incorrectly.
